lane: SP1-TD1 verifier trust target + canonical program identity

canonicalProcedureScripts.provenance: the workstation (environment B) driver; never committed by SP1-P1. Last modified 8 s before the measured B run's output directory out-20261015T040434Z, and it copies in the same host-build-in-container.sh (identical sha256) that the runner used

measurementScriptsNotCommitted.reason: this repository's CodeQL security-extended configuration analyzes every JavaScript path outside build directories, and four of these scripts send file-derived data over the network, which it raises as new alerts; to leave the analyzed surface unchanged none of the five JavaScript measurement scripts is committed. Their exact bytes are published on the pull request. The chain-state, deployment-bytecode, chain-execution and route-timeline observations record the sha256 of the script that produced them, the local-remap observation records to-observation.cjs, and chain-execution names the mainnet-proof observation it wrote; the upstream fixture's extractor is identified by hash on the pull request only, and the image digests are re-derivable from the public registry (vendor-image.raw.json, method)

options.label: ZKMLDSAVerifier bound directly to the immutable SP1Verifier v6.1.0, pinned by runtime code hash
options.newAttackSurface: none added: the consumer already calls ISP1Verifier; the pin is one EXTCODEHASH comparison at construction
options.operationalComplexity: a new wrapper per SP1 circuit release, applied through the vault's timelocked pqVerifier rotation; WalletWall watches upstream advisories and gateway freezes as signals

options.label: A, plus fail-closed when the upstream gateway freezes the pinned selector (read-only coupling)
options.newAttackSurface: one read of the gateway's route table per verification; a per-chain gateway address
options.operationalComplexity: as A, plus the gateway address per chain; a routine upstream deprecation freeze of v6.1.0 stops verification until WalletWall rotates

options.label: Succinct's gateway, with WalletWall pinning the selector, the route's verifier and both code hashes
options.newAttackSurface: a pinning layer plus the gateway's routing code in the accepted path; per-chain gateway addresses
options.operationalComplexity: per-chain gateway address and route check at deployment; the same per-release redeploy as A

options.label: Succinct's gateway with a selector-only pin (the naive variant)
options.newAttackSurface: fails open on any chain where the pinned selector is not yet routed: the owner registers any verifier under it
options.operationalComplexity: as B, without the checks that make it safe

options.label: A WalletWall-owned instance of the gateway code
options.newAttackSurface: a second, instant verifier-replacement path that bypasses PQ_VERIFIER_UPDATE_DELAY and GOVERNANCE_GRACE_PERIOD
options.operationalComplexity: a new privileged key or Safe to operate and monitor; route hygiene per chain

options.label: Succinct's gateway, unpinned (what docs/ZK_Prover_Runbook.md section 4 directs today)
path: any live route the prover selects
options.newAttackSurface: every live route on every chain is in the accepted relation, including deprecated or release-candidate verifiers
options.operationalComplexity: lowest: one address per chain, upgrades without WalletWall action

candidates.role: cross-check only (pre-registered: depends on a separately installed toolchain and the builder's own path)

commands: git archive --format=tar HEAD zkvm/guest zkvm/host (the subject; no other files)
docker create --platform linux/amd64 <image@digest>; docker cp the archive and the entrypoint in; no bind mounts, no cache volumes

in the container: cargo build --release --locked in /root/program/zkvm/host (locks the HOST's dependencies; build.rs -> sp1_build::build_program builds the guest in local mode inside the image WITHOUT --locked, see guestLock)
in the container: the host's own `vkey` / `acvp-vkey` on the ELFs it embedded
outside every build environment: cargo-prove vkey --elf on each ELF file (vkey cross-check)

environment.network: crates.io for the --locked crate set (checksums from Cargo.lock)

forbidden: a mutable image tag (sp1-build --docker --tag pulls by tag)
a developer CARGO_HOME, RUSTFLAGS or CARGO_TARGET_DIR
canonicalProcedure.guestLock: required: the canonical workflow must leave zkvm/guest/Cargo.lock unchanged by the build (git diff --exit-code after building) or pass BuildArgs.locked = true; sp1-build 6.3.1's build_program defaults to locked = false. The measured host-flow ELFs equal the --locked docker-mode ELFs on both hosts, so the designated identity is unaffected

offChainLivenessDependencies: Groth16 proof generation for circuit v6.1.0 needs Succinct's v6.1.0 circuit artifacts (about 6.21 GB) or the Succinct prover network; integrity is checked on chain by the pinned verifier key, availability is not WalletWall's.
Rebuilding the canonical ELF needs the vendor image (ghcr.io, by digest) and crates.io for the locked crate set; the digest and Cargo.lock checksums protect integrity, not availability.
A PqOnly user's exit during the 2-day rotation window needs a proof, so the timelock protects them only while proving is available (TD1-N9).

findings.title: uint64(block.chainid) truncation in ZKMLDSAVerifier.verify
findings.practicalImpact: none: every measured or targeted chain id is far below 2^64, and every consumer's EIP-712 digest binds the full 256-bit chainid (WalletWallVault, WalletWallMultiSigVault, PolicyControlBridge and StablecoinVaultSimulator all use _hashTypedDataV4)
findings.securityImpact: the journal chain_id is prover-chosen stdin the guest never checks, so it is a proof-routing tag, not a binding; authorization binds chain identity only through the digest. The truncation makes the verifier's own tag compare modulo 2^64.
findings.plan: implementation lane: compare uint256(committedChainId) with block.chainid (fail closed at or above 2^64); a contract-only change, no guest, ELF or vkey change

findings.title: journal sigHash not checked on chain
findings.securityImpact: authorization is 'the key behind pkHash signed exactly this digest'; any valid signature over the digest authorizes, and replay is prevented by the digest's nonce and deadline, so no authorization fact depends on which signature was used. No document claims the ZK path binds the signature hash (those claims describe AttestationPQCVerifier).
findings.plan: document sigHash as non-authoritative in the implementation lane; removing it would change the guest, ELF, vkey and journal ABI for no security gain

findings.title: 'immutable trust root' conflates address and relation immutability
findings.practicalImpact: misleading operator guidance while the runbook points at the gateway
findings.securityImpact: the accepted relation is immutable only if no principal other than WalletWall's timelocked rotation can widen it; an immutable address in front of a mutable route table is not
findings.plan: implementation lane rewrites docs/ZK_Verifier_Production.md and the runbook section 4 in these terms (both are bytes the SP1-P1 STOP receipt binds; see TD1-N4)

findings.title: testnet gateway owned by one EOA with a live release-candidate route
findings.practicalImpact: on Sepolia and Base Sepolia (TD1-N5) one key controls the route table and v4.0.0-rc.3 is live
findings.securityImpact: a single key can widen every unpinned consumer on both testnets; acceptable only for no-value experiments that name that key as an authority, and unnecessary because the same immutable v6.1.0 code is deployed at the same address there
findings.plan: testnet deployments bind directly to v6.1.0 like production; no testnet exception

findings.title: SP1-P1's route history from the Blockscout indexer was incomplete
findings.practicalImpact: the Sepolia RouteFrozen for v5.0.0 (block 11874717) is in the RPC receipt but absent from Blockscout's logs for that transaction
findings.securityImpact: enumerating a mutable route table from an indexer is not a completeness proof; under the TD1 design no route outside the pinned code identity matters
findings.plan: none needed beyond recording it; SP1-P1's frozen receipt is not rewritten

findings.title: SP1-P1 recorded the v6.1.1 tag as lightweight
findings.practicalImpact: v6.1.1 is an annotated tag carrying a PGP signature block (unverified here); v6.0.0 and v6.1.0 are lightweight
findings.securityImpact: none on the decision: provenance rests on byte equality, CREATE2 and code-hash measurements, not on tag signatures

findings.title: one key spans testnet sole ownership and a mainnet Safe seat
findings.practicalImpact: 0xBaB2c2aF5b91695e65955DA60d63aD1b2aE81126 is the sole owner on Sepolia and Base Sepolia and one of the three signers of the 2-of-3 Safe on Ethereum and Base
findings.securityImpact: its compromise grants full testnet route control and half of the mainnet threshold; relevant only to options that leave the gateway owner in the accepted path
findings.plan: none for WalletWall under the TD1 design

findings.title: the SP1-P1 STOP validator is a live tripwire on the files the next lane must change
findings.practicalImpact: validate:sp1-p1-receipt binds the sha256 of contracts/verifiers/ZKMLDSAVerifier.sol and requires the runbook to direct SP1_VERIFIER_ADDRESS at the gateway
findings.securityImpact: none; but restamping a spent STOP receipt would erase what it proved
findings.plan: implementation lane marks the SP1-P1 receipt superseded (historical bindings) instead of restamping it

findings.title: Base Sepolia mirrors Sepolia's posture
findings.practicalImpact: the gateway on WalletWall's second testnet is owned by the same single EOA and also routes v4.0.0-rc.3 live

findings.title: upstream freezes are discretionary: fast for a broken build, a deprecation batch for an advised version
findings.practicalImpact: the broken first v6.1.0 build was frozen on Sepolia 21.4 hours after it was routed; the advised v6.0.0 route (GHSA-63x8-x938-vx33, 2026-04-11) was frozen on mainnet 181 days later, 108 s after the unaffected v5.0.0 route, i.e. as a deprecation batch
findings.securityImpact: a freeze is dual-use: it stops valid proofs (liveness) and, when the verifier itself is unsound, forged ones (protection). Its timing is upstream's choice, and a routine deprecation freeze is near-certain over a deployment's life. Whether WalletWall couples to it is an explicit owner decision (DEFECT_RESPONSE_COUPLING), not a property this lane can settle. TD1 claims no exploitability of the on-chain v6.0.0 verifier.
findings.plan: decided 2026-10-15: WALLETWALL_DETECT_AND_FAIL_CLOSED, as a local one-way halt at the verifier wrapper; upstream signals are detection evidence only and never a WalletWall authority

findings.title: the host flow builds the guest without --locked
findings.practicalImpact: zkvm/host/build.rs calls sp1_build::build_program, whose BuildArgs.locked defaults to false; the host's --locked does not reach the nested guest build. The measured host-flow ELFs equal the --locked docker-mode ELFs on both hosts
findings.securityImpact: a stale guest lockfile would re-resolve from crates.io silently instead of failing; the designated identity is unaffected
findings.plan: canonical workflow: assert zkvm/guest/Cargo.lock unchanged after the build, or build with BuildArgs.locked = true

findings.title: the same code hash is not the same relation on a chain whose precompiles differ
findings.practicalImpact: the Groth16 verifier ANDs the pairing call's success with the first output word; on a chain without the 0x08 precompile the call succeeds and the word is still the first input word, so an odd word passes. The odd-word canary reverts, and a real v6.1.0 proof verifies, on all four measured chains
findings.securityImpact: the code-hash pin is necessary, not sufficient; precompile semantics are chain-governed (an L2's upgrade keys can change them), an implicit authority every option shares
findings.plan: deploy tooling: per-chain execution check (real proof accepted, tampered and odd-word canary refused) before deploying, and periodically after

findings.title: the rotation delay protects PqOnly users only if they can prove within it
findings.practicalImpact: the 2-day pqVerifier rotation gives users time to exit, but a PqOnly exit needs a proof, i.e. Succinct's v6.1.0 artifacts or prover network during that window
findings.securityImpact: the timelock's protection depends on an off-chain liveness dependency
findings.plan: archive the v6.1.0 circuit artifacts by hash and keep a self-hosted proving path before real value

findings.title: four consumers verify through the PQ verifier, each with its own fail-closed holder
findings.practicalImpact: under A, failing closed on a verifier defect takes the pause() of every vault deployment (owner-held) and the policy bridge's one-way pause() (EMERGENCY_PAUSER); pausing a vault does not stop the bridge, which reads the consumer's pqVerifier
findings.securityImpact: a soundness defect in the pinned verifier stays exploitable through any consumer whose holder has not acted
findings.plan: decided: one local, one-way halt at the verifier wrapper, applied to every consumer that can recover from it (WalletWallVault, StablecoinVaultSimulator and PolicyControlBridge; WalletWallMultiSigVault only after TD2-MULTISIG-ROTATION), built and tested in TD2

findings.title: WalletWallMultiSigVault has no verifier rotation and no exit that avoids PQ verification
findings.practicalImpact: its pqVerifier is set once in the constructor and withdraw() needs at least one PQ signature through it, so a one-way halt of its wrapper would lock its funds: the decided recovery (a new wrapper and the timelocked rotation) does not exist for it
findings.securityImpact: none for authorization; a permanent liveness loss for that consumer if its wrapper is halted
findings.plan: TD2-MULTISIG-ROTATION: the halt is not applied to WalletWallMultiSigVault until it has an explicit delayed pqVerifier replacement path (a new authorization capability for its owner, accounted and reviewed separately); until then it is bound to no part of the SP1 path and its owner's pause is its only fail-closed lever; real value stays blocked, for every consumer, until both that path and the common halt are built and tested

findings.title: while a wrapper is halted, the rotation delay gives no one an exit
findings.practicalImpact: every PQ-gated withdrawal fails while the wrapper is halted (WalletWallVault and StablecoinVaultSimulator in PqOnly or Hybrid mode, and every multisig vault, whose pqThreshold is at least one), so those users cannot leave during the 172,800 s rotation that recovery runs through; guardian recovery replaces credentials but withdraws nothing; today's rotation accepts any code-bearing target
findings.securityImpact: during recovery the rotation target is the vault owner's choice alone, unchecked by exit; for the multisig vault an accept-all target would leave each withdrawal guarded by its tenant's ECDSA signatures alone
findings.plan: TD2 states whether recovery-target gating (only a wrapper whose code hash and PROGRAM_VKEY designation passed the SP1 evidence gates) is enforced on chain or by process, tests it, and counts the answer in the authorization cut: for the multisig vault in TD2-MULTISIG-ROTATION (an unacceptable cut stops it), for the vaults in scope in the cut reported to the owner

implementationPlan: ZKMLDSAVerifier: compile-time pin of the SP1 verifier's runtime code hash (and record VERIFIER_HASH, VK_ROOT, VERSION) checked in the constructor; keep the verify() logic unchanged
ZKMLDSAVerifier: compare uint256(committedChainId) with block.chainid (F-1); document sigHash as non-authoritative (F-2)

Defect response (decided 2026-10-15: WALLETWALL_DETECT_AND_FAIL_CLOSED via LOCAL_ONE_WAY_VERIFIER_HALT), as TD2-COMMON-VERIFIER-HALT: a halt at the WalletWall verifier wrapper with ACTIVE -> HALTED only; a halt-only principal (an existing emergency-security authority if it already satisfies the separation, else a new threshold or multisig; no rotation, vkey, upgrade or unhalt power, also after any ownership transfer); upstream signals as detection evidence only; recovery only by a new wrapper and the timelocked rotation, never to a fresh deployment of the halted identity; applied to WalletWallVault, StablecoinVaultSimulator and PolicyControlBridge, tested through each (valid verification while ACTIVE, the same verification fails closed after HALTED, the halt principal cannot make an invalid proof valid); deployment tooling refuses a haltable wrapper to WalletWallMultiSigVault until TD2-MULTISIG-ROTATION

TD2-MULTISIG-ROTATION (prerequisite for applying the halt to WalletWallMultiSigVault): an explicit delayed pqVerifier replacement path (at least the repository's 172,800 s), targeting only a new wrapper that has passed the SP1 evidence gates; no instantaneous replacement; no halt principal may invoke it; no HALTED -> ACTIVE on the old wrapper, and no fresh deployment of the halted identity as the target; executable proofs (halted then rotated, the same valid authorization succeeds; a malicious or accept-all replacement cannot be activated outside the delayed path; the halt principal cannot rotate); a recalculated authorization cut, never labelled authority-neutral, that accounts for the missing exit while halted (TD1-N12); STOP and return to design if that cut is unacceptable
Designation file for mldsa65-withdrawal (generated from build observations, never typed) plus a CI check that fails when the zkvm subject no longer matches it

A gated canonical-build workflow (vendor image by digest; guest lockfile unchanged after the build, TD1-N7) and a second-host release rebuild; both ELF and vkey must equal the designation, vkey recomputed by cargo-prove outside the build

scripts/deploy-zk-verifier.ts: take PROGRAM_VKEY only from the designation and the SP1 verifier only from the trust-target designation, check EXTCODEHASH and run the per-chain execution check (real proof accepted, tampered and odd-word canary refused) on the target chain, refuse overrides on non-local chains, read back after deployment
Docs: rewrite the runbook section 4 and ZK_Verifier_Production.md in the TD1 terms (F-3); mark the SP1-P1 STOP receipt superseded rather than restamped (TD1-N4)
Proving availability: archive the v6.1.0 circuit artifacts by hash (their groth16_vk.bin sha256 must equal VERIFIER_HASH) and keep a self-hosted proving path (TD1-N9)

ownerDecisions.question: If the pinned verifier itself proves unsound, what stops verification first?

choices.description: no upstream lever in the accepted path. WalletWall detects (upstream advisories, gateway RouteFrozen events, CVEs, verifier-repository disclosures and watcher findings are evidence only) and fails every consumer of the verifier that can recover from it closed through one local, one-way, halt-only circuit breaker at the verifier wrapper (a consumer that cannot, WalletWallMultiSigVault, waits outside it for TD2-MULTISIG-ROTATION); recovery only by a new wrapper and the timelocked rotation

not chosen. AF: A's direct binding plus a read-only check of the upstream gateway's freeze bit for the pinned selector; upstream's freeze would fail every consumer closed at once, at the cost of making the gateway owners a WalletWall liveness principal on every chain, tied to one gateway instance. B realizes the same coupling through the gateway's routing code (same principals, longer path) and is not offered

ownerDecisions.rationale: owner decision 2026-10-15: keep the direct binding to the immutable, code-pinned SP1 v6.1.0 verifier, with no dependency on the Succinct gateway for authorization or automatic liveness control; fail closed through a local, one-way, halt-only circuit breaker at the WalletWall verifier wrapper, so every consumer (PolicyControlBridge included) fails closed through one mechanism; recover only through the explicit replacement path. AF (UPSTREAM_FREEZE_FAIL_CLOSED) is not chosen, and upstream signals never become a WalletWall authority; amended the same day (TD1-N11 a prerequisite): the halt applies only to consumers that can recover from it, and WalletWallMultiSigVault waits outside it for TD2-MULTISIG-ROTATION

haltPrincipal.selection: prefer an existing WalletWall emergency-security authority that already satisfies the separation (the PolicyControlBridge EMERGENCY_PAUSER role pattern: halt-only and one-way); otherwise a new authority scoped to the halt; threshold or multisig control preferred over a single online EOA; never the vault owner (holds the pqVerifier rotation and a reversible pause), never the upstream gateway owner

td2Tests: positive control, through each consumer in the halt's scope (WalletWallVault, StablecoinVaultSimulator and PolicyControlBridge): a valid verification succeeds while ACTIVE

after HALTED, the same otherwise-valid verification fails closed through every consumer in the scope; WalletWallMultiSigVault joins the scope only through TD2-MULTISIG-ROTATION, with its own halted-then-rotated proof

adversarial: no action of the halt principal makes an invalid proof valid, changes SP1_VERIFIER or PROGRAM_VKEY, selects another verifier, adds or removes a route, invokes a rotation (also after any ownership transfer), bypasses verification or restores it
no transition out of HALTED exists, and no upstream signal (RouteFrozen, advisory, CVE, disclosure, watcher finding) moves the state

recovery only by a new wrapper with independently established verifier and program identity, through the normal evidence gates and the timelocked rotation; a fresh deployment of the halted identity is refused as a recovery target
negative: binding WalletWallMultiSigVault to a haltable wrapper is refused (deployment tooling), until TD2-MULTISIG-ROTATION

amendments.summary: the halt must not be applied to WalletWallMultiSigVault until it has a recoverable verifier transition (TD2-MULTISIG-ROTATION, frozen); recovery is not claimed for all four consumers; the halt principal, the multisig vault's owner and the proposed multisig rotation are accounted apart; real value waits for the rotation path and the common halt, both built and tested

the owner keeps both additions of the amendment's review as frozen TD2 requirements, binding like the owner's own items: one-way per identity (a fresh deployment of the halted identity is refused as a recovery or rotation target) and the halt principal cannot rotate, also after an ownership transfer

vaultOwnerToday.note: each WalletWallVault and StablecoinVaultSimulator deployment's owner: its timelocked pqVerifier rotation (172,800 s; the recovery path for the consumers in the halt's scope) is the governed lever the decision retains, and its pause is reversible. The halt principal is never this principal

multisigOwnerToday.note: the onlyOwner functions it declares are pause() and unpause() (the inherited Ownable2Step transfer hands over only these; renounceOwnership is disabled); it cannot change the verifier, which is set once in the constructor

proposedMultisigRotation.note: the contract's single owner could, after the delay, point the vault at any verifier, an accept-all one included, voiding every tenant's p-of-q PQ signatures at once and leaving each withdrawal guarded by the tenant's m-of-n ECDSA signatures alone. While the old wrapper is halted no tenant can withdraw at all (every exit needs a PQ signature), so the delay gives no exit during recovery and the target gating is the only check (TD1-N12). That is a widening lever even though its holder already exists, so it is not authority-neutral; TD2 recalculates this cut and stops if it is unacceptable

td2Requirements.summary: build the local one-way verifier halt at the WalletWall wrapper and test it through every consumer in its scope (see haltDesign.td2Tests)
reviewAdditions: the exclusion is enforced, not only stated: deployment tooling refuses to bind a consumer kept outside the halt to a haltable wrapper, with a negative test; until its gate WalletWallMultiSigVault is bound to no part of the SP1 path (any other interim, such as a non-haltable pinned wrapper, is an owner decision)
a fresh deployment of the halted identity (the same SP1 verifier code hash and PROGRAM_VKEY) is refused as a recovery target: a halt is one-way for the identity, not only for the wrapper instance
the halt principal cannot rotate, also after any ownership transfer: TD2 states whether code or an operational check enforces it, and tests it

TD1-N12: while a wrapper is halted the rotation delay gives no exit, so TD2 states whether recovery-target gating is enforced on chain or by process for the vaults in scope, and counts the answer in the authorization cut it reports to the owner

td2Requirements.summary: give WalletWallMultiSigVault a recoverable verifier transition before the halt may be applied to it
items: design and implement an explicit delayed pqVerifier replacement path for WalletWallMultiSigVault
prefer the repository's existing 172,800-second verifier-rotation semantics unless independent review establishes a stronger compatible mechanism
rotation must target a new wrapper whose verifier code hash and PROGRAM_VKEY designation have already passed the SP1 evidence gates
no halt principal may invoke rotation
no HALTED -> ACTIVE transition on the old wrapper

executably prove that after the old wrapper is halted the MultiSig cannot withdraw through it, and that after the authorized delay and a rotation to a fresh valid wrapper the same valid authorization succeeds
prove that a malicious or accept-all replacement cannot be activated outside the authorized delayed path
recalculate the authorization cut introduced by giving the MultiSig administrative authority verifier-rotation power; do not label it authority-neutral merely because the principal already existed
keep real-value readiness blocked until this recovery path and the common verifier halt are both implemented and tested
reviewAdditions: the recalculated cut accounts for TD1-N12: while the old wrapper is halted no tenant can withdraw, so the delay gives no exit and the target gating (item 3) is the only check; TD2 states whether that gating is enforced on chain or by process
a fresh deployment of the halted identity is refused as a rotation target (item 6 at the level of the identity)
the halt principal cannot rotate, also after any ownership transfer (item 5 made executable)

stopCondition.text: if adding verifier rotation to WalletWallMultiSigVault creates an unacceptable authorization cut, STOP TD2-MULTISIG-ROTATION and return to design rather than weakening the one-way halt
